title: Privacy.
summary: Privacy information for An AUsome Life.
search: Site information · updated October 16, 2026Privacy.Useful tools, with clear choices about your words and pictures.The current websiteAn AUsome Life is a static website hosted through GitHub Pages. We do not operate visitor accounts, checkout, comments, a public upload gallery or an on-site contact form. We do not currently use our own advertising cookies or behavioral analytics.GitHub states that GitHub Pages logs visitors’ IP addresses for security. Read GitHub’s explanation. Page and image requests still reach the hosting provider even when a tool processes your input locally.Picture cards & visit plansWords typed into the picture-card and visit-plan editors and photos selected from your device are processed in the open browser tab. These tools do not send that text or those photos to us or an image provider, and they do not save your edited plan on our server. Save or print before closing or reloading.A saved PNG or PDF becomes a file on the device or in the destination you choose. The website cannot delete those copies. On a shared device, close the editing tab and consider where downloaded files and print jobs are kept.Public event or place links may prefill a plan using information in the link. URLs can appear in browser history and hosting logs, so do not put private names, care information or other sensitive details into a shared URL.Reading tools & your preferencesText size, color, spacing, motion and other reading choices apply in the current page without being sent to us. If you turn on “Remember my choices on this device,” those choices are saved in this browser’s local storage for other pages and later visits. We do not infer or ask for a disability or diagnosis. Uncheck the option or choose “Reset all choices” to remove the saved preferences. Leave it off on a shared device.Reading view prepares the visible page text in your browser. It leaves forms and editable inputs on the original page. Copying or printing sends the text only to the clipboard or print destination you choose.The reading-view “Read aloud” control lists only voices the browser identifies as local to the device. It does not send reading text to this website or request a remote voice. Voice availability and behavior depend on your browser and device. Listening starts when you choose it and stops when reading view is closed.Open reading tools and helpImage prompts & future generationThe image-prompt helper prepares text for you to copy. “Copy prompt & open ChatGPT” places that text on your clipboard and opens ChatGPT; it does not submit your prompt. If you paste it into a separate AI service, that service’s privacy and retention terms apply. Use a general description when a person’s name, diagnosis or private address is unnecessary.This site does not currently research or generate a new image live for a visitor. Before a live service is introduced, we will explain what is sent, which providers process it, how long it is retained and what choices you have. Your local photos will not be silently sent as references.External services & contactOpening a map, retailer, social account or video preview takes you to another service. An activated video player may load content from that provider. Those services have their own privacy practices. Other spoken-content tools you choose outside this website follow your browser or operating system’s settings and privacy practices.If you email us, the email providers process the information you choose to send. We use it to respond and address the matter raised. Please leave private care records and unnecessary identifying details out of an initial message.Questions or privacy concerns? Contact the editor. This page will be updated when the site’s data practices change.

title: A little lake time.
summary: Fall foliage, lakeside boats and a rainbow: a lovely Rangeley, Maine getaway from our family's photo album, with practical notes for planning a visit.
search: The journalRangeley, MaineA grandparents’ field note The rainbow rather stole the show. From the family camera roll, Rangeley, Maine. Fall in the western Maine mountainsA little lake time.The grandparents, some downtime in Rangeley, and a very good reason to stop looking at the clock.October 6, 2026Mom-Mom & Grandpa Steve (aka Grandma & Grandpa) got a little time away in Maine. The photographs have all the ingredients I love: fall color, boats at the dock, a dog by the water, and a sky doing something magnificent.Grandparents deserve a chapter like this, too. The grandparents’ pauseMap & placesAccess & sensory notes From their corner of the lakeA day with room around it.There is something especially lovely about seeing the grandparents get a bit of downtime. We have plenty of family stories with a destination, a departure time, and several people’s needs to fit into the day. This little Rangeley chapter gets to be about a pause.Look at that shoreline: the boats tucked along the docks, the hills turning gold and rust, the ducks gathered near the grass. In one photograph, dark clouds sit above the village and a rainbow lands almost neatly behind it. Maine has apparently decided to handle the decorations.I love the ordinary part just as much. A jacket, a dog on a lead, a few minutes by the water. The sort of scene you might walk past while trying to get somewhere else—and then realize it was the thing you wanted all along. A little company at the water’s edge. The ducks appear to have called a meeting. A lakeside pause. Original editorial illustration inspired by a Maine landscape, not a map of the visit.The good partLet the view be the outing.A beautiful place does not need a very ambitious plan. For a grandparent getaway—or anyone whose idea of a holiday includes sitting down—I like the thought of choosing one lovely place and leaving time to enjoy it.A lake view can be the whole afternoon.That is the feeling I want to keep from these photographs: a little breathing room, a little fall color, and the people we love getting a turn to enjoy both.A broad sky, a patch of sunshine, and plenty to look at. Pictures to take with youA few words for this story.Choose the pictures that are familiar and useful. Change a label, save a card, or print this little set.canoeDownload PNG ↓life jacketDownload PNG ↓waterDownload PNG ↓breakDownload PNG ↓Edit or print this set →All picture cards →Keep the person’s usual communication available. These are independent picture communication cards, not official PECS® materials. Generic place illustrations do not show a venue’s actual layout.A small guide to your own lake timeRangeley, at your pace.These are researched options for planning your own visit. The family photographs above show the grandparents’ getaway; the places below have their own facilities and access conditions.Open the Rangeley mapThe map is for regional orientation. Check the route from parking to your chosen seat, viewpoint or restroom with the site operator. For a lakeside picnicRangeley Lake State Park. Maine lists day-use parking, restrooms and picnic tables as accessible; the picnic area as generally accessible; the beach as accessible with assistance; and the trails as not accessible. Ask staff which route best fits your needs.The published day-use season is May 1–October 15, 9 a.m. to sunset. Off-season facilities close and entry is on foot from outside the gate, which changes the outing considerably.Park information & current notices · Official access ratings In-season questions: 207-864-3858 For the view, with less walkingQuill Hill. The operator describes a four-mile dirt road to the summit, parking at the top and panoramic views. That makes it an option to investigate when a mountain hike is not the plan. Ask about the surface between parking and the viewpoint, seating, and restroom arrangements.The site’s seasonal notices vary between “through October” and “mid-October.” Confirm the gate is open before setting out; cars, motorcycles and ATVs also use the road.Quill Hill updates · Official directions For a gentle wander, if it suitsHatchery Brook Preserve. Rangeley Lakes Heritage Trust describes easy walking near the village, waterfront picnic spots and stretches of bog bridging. “Easy” does not establish wheelchair access: ask about widths, transitions, wet surfaces and the distance to a comfortable turning point.Preserve details & trail map Trail questions: 207-864-7311 The useful detailsMake the pause comfortable. Look beyond “waterfront.”For a stay, ask for the actual route from the car to the room and the lake view. Check steps, slopes, firm surfaces, bathroom layout, bed height and a place to sit with a backrest. The grassy slope and shoreline rocks visible in these photos are a useful reminder that a lovely view and an easy route are separate questions. Plan for sound, light and weather.Open water can mean wind, glare and boat noise; a scenic overlook can bring engines and conversation. Ask when a place tends to be quieter, bring familiar sensory supports if useful, and choose a stop with an easy return to shelter. A photograph cannot tell us how quiet a place felt. Keep the water’s edge optional.Enjoying a lake need not involve a dock or a boat. Choose a stable place to sit back from the edge. If close supervision around water is part of your family’s routine, build that into the plan. For a boat outing, ask separately about boarding, transfers and suitable life jackets. Give the dog—and the ducks—space.Check pet rules for the specific property and outing. Keep your dog close on a lead, leave wildlife room, and watch the ducks without feeding them. A pet-friendly listing is also worth checking for room restrictions and fees before booking. Before you leaveThe small, sensible list.Choose one main stop and confirm its seasonal opening.Check parking, the walking or rolling surface, a seat and an open restroom.Bring a warm layer, rain protection, water and something familiar to eat.Save directions before setting out and keep the return plan simple.Leave enough room in the day to stay a little longer—or finish early. For this field note, I keep coming back to the rainbow. The grandparents got their lake time, and we got these photographs to enjoy. A very good little chapter.Family photographs supplied for this story. Regional planning information checked October 6, 2026 against the linked official sources.
